Read the front view as maximum heights by left-to-right column: [1, 3, 3, 1]. Read the right view, aligned with the top view rows, as maximum heights by row top-to-bottom: [3, 3, 2, 1] (the displayed right-view order is the corresponding side projection). For each occupied footprint cell, the greatest possible stack height is the smaller of its front-column maximum and its right-row maximum. Fill every occupied position to this bound and check that each front column and each right-row maximum is still achieved. The height table becomes: row 1 = 3,3; row 2 = 3,3,1; row 3 = 1,2,2; row 4 = 1. Summing gives 3+3+3+3+1+1+2+2+1 = 19.
